P1.source_and_assumptions: Read physical pp.4-5 Eqs.(11)-(19), p.17 A.4, actual p.18 Eq.(63), p.22 A.9. The general model allows arbitrary regular deterministic linear f,h,g and positive finite penalty. It does not require the hard-endpoint law or gamma infinity for Eq.(18). Original text explicitly introduces a stochastic interpolant but continues to identify it as the controlled forward transition.
P1.independent_derivation: For f=h=0,g=1,T=gamma=1, the controlled drift is (1-X)/(2-t). Variance ODE v'=-2v/(2-t)+1 is solved by v=t(2-t)/2; at .5 this is3/8, while printed t(1-t)=1/4. In general d_t'=-exp(2F_T)exp(-2F_t)g_t^2, so fundamental-solution integration gives exp(2F_t)d_t^2 int exp(-2F_s)g_s^2/d_s^2 ds=exp(2F_t)G_t^2 d_t/d_0. This establishes covariance independently of the initial verdict.
P1.transition_and_terminal: For T=10,gamma=.1,s=8,t=9, a_t/a_s=11/12 and printed innovation .9-1.6*(11/12)^2=-4/9 at regular interior times. The GOU scalar terminal variance is S/(1+gamma*S), so x0=y=0 has positive MSE .463710558 rather than a deterministic zero. Point-target W2-squared equals that second moment.
P1.alternatives_and_scope: An arbitrary hybrid interpolant can be defined, but cannot inherit the same drift/joint conditional; Eq.(63) itself can fail positivity. Gamma infinity and deterministic mean survive; near-hard release defaults and t=100 special cases prevent inferring default NaNs or false image-quality scores. Static code confirms finite-gamma mean plus gamma-independent variance and training times1..99.
P1.severity_and_repair: Major central SOC-to-training distribution derivation. Replace covariance and rederive transitions/reverse sampling, or separately derive consistent interpolant dynamics. Only moment law is verified; no repaired full algorithm/performance certified.

P2.source_and_check: Actual p.5 declared score=-epsilon/sigma_prime and Eq.(19) plus term; actual p.6 Algorithms1-2 visibly use plus epsilon/(sigma_prime)^2; p.19 Eq.(66) substitution corroborates. Backward step -Delta(b-g^2 score) adds Delta*g^2*score=-Delta*g^2 epsilon/sigma_prime. For g=1,sigma=.5,epsilon=1 values -2,+2,+4 follow.
P2.alternatives_and_scope: Changing noise sign would contradict the declared score and does not fix extra denominator power. Static score=-noise/f_sigma, drift b-g^2 score and subtraction of drift give consistent release convention, so no implementation sign bug is established.
P2.severity_and_repair: Minor bounded printed convention inconsistency distinct from covariance defect; correct sign, standard-deviation denominator and timestep factors. No empirical failure or historical-code provenance is inferred.
